hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap as needs outpace available money
hero.teaser: Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall, and the gap between what the county needs and what it can afford could shape how residents get around for decades.
hero.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next 20 years, a gap that could determine how residents travel for decades to come.

The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements through 2050, but only $701 million is currently available. That means the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Nearly all of the available funding comes from state and federal sources, with only $10 million coming from local revenue. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August and outlines transportation needs across roads, transit, aviation, freight, and other infrastructure categories.

Among the most pressing unfunded needs are nine roads the county identified as requiring widening as traffic grows. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, money that is not currently available, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. Without funding for these widening projects, the county will be unable to address growing congestion on these corridors.

State Road 710 stands out as among the county's highest priorities and has been the subject of repeated safety concerns. About $300 million in projects are planned for the corridor, reflecting the urgent need for improvements on this route. The massive funding shortfall highlights the challenge facing Martin County as it tries to balance transportation demands with limited financial resources over the coming decades.

cards.headline: Boca Raton man arrested for soliciting videos from 14-year-old, Boynton Beach police seek additional victims
cards.teaser: Maximiliano Buitrago of Boca Raton was arrested after allegedly asking a 14-year-old for videos in response to a Craigslist babysitting post.
cards.body:
A Boca Raton man faces serious charges after allegedly soliciting videos from someone he believed to be a 14-year-old girl, according to Boynton Beach police. Maximiliano Buitrago, 51, was arrested on charges of solicitation to commit human trafficking and unlawful use of a two-way communication device. Investigators say Buitrago responded to a Craigslist advertisement offering summer babysitting services that had been posted by undercover detectives from the Human Exploitation Unit. He allegedly asked, "Are you trying to make cash any other way? What else can you do?"

According to police, Buitrago repeatedly acknowledged during their communications that he understood the person was 14 years old. He allegedly offered to pay the minor for videos, claiming they would be shown to clients overseas. The suspect continued the conversation with the undercover detective, eventually arranging to meet in person.

On July 16, Buitrago set up a meeting with who he thought was the teenage girl at a park in Boynton Beach. When he arrived at the location, officers took him into custody. During a search of his vehicle, police discovered cards that read, "Make money on TikTok with pics and short videos," which also included an offer to "get paid cash." The discovery of these cards raised concerns among investigators that Buitrago may have approached other young people with similar propositions.

Buitrago confessed to investigators following his arrest and is currently being held at the Palm Beach County jail. Boynton Beach police believe there could be additional victims who may have encountered the suspect. Authorities are asking anyone who might have received one of the cards found in Buitrago's vehicle or who may have communicated with him to come forward. Anyone with information is urged to contact BBPD Detective Joseph at 561-742-6158. The case highlights ongoing efforts by law enforcement to identify and arrest individuals who attempt to exploit minors, particularly through online platforms and social media. The Human Exploitation Unit's undercover operation successfully intercepted Buitrago before he could potentially harm an actual minor.

cards.headline: Three women arrested in alleged $7 million fraud scheme targeting St. Lucie County business
cards.teaser: Three women face arrest in connection with an alleged $7 million fraud investigation involving a St. Lucie County business.
cards.body:
Three women were arrested Friday in connection with an alleged $7 million fraud scheme targeting a St. Lucie County business. The investigation centers on allegations of luxury car purchases and vacations funded through the fraudulent activity.

The women face charges related to the alleged scheme that resulted in $7 million missing from the St. Lucie County business. Law enforcement investigated the fraud case before making the arrests Friday.

Authorities say the investigation revealed purchases of luxury vehicles and vacation travel connected to the alleged fraud. The three suspects were taken into custody in St. Lucie County.

cards.headline: Orlando man arrested after Juno Beach child sex abuse investigation
cards.teaser: An Orlando man faces arrest following a child sex abuse investigation conducted in Juno Beach.
cards.body:
An Orlando man was arrested Friday following a child sex abuse investigation in Juno Beach. The investigation led to the arrest of the suspect from Orlando.

Juno Beach authorities conducted the investigation that resulted in the Friday arrest. The man now faces charges related to child sex abuse.

Law enforcement completed the investigation before taking the Orlando resident into custody. The case involved allegations of child sex abuse in Juno Beach.

cards.headline: Four arrested after holding gun to Florida teen's head, pushing him from car
cards.teaser: Four people were arrested after deputies say they held a gun to a Florida teenager's head and pushed him out of a moving vehicle.
cards.body:
Four people were arrested Friday after deputies say they held a gun to a Florida teenager's head and pushed him out of a car. The incident involved a teen victim who was forced from the vehicle.

Deputies say the suspects held a gun to the teen's head during the incident before pushing him out of the car. The four suspects were taken into custody following the Friday incident.

Law enforcement arrested all four individuals involved in the alleged crime against the teenager. The suspects now face charges related to the armed assault and forced removal of the victim from the vehicle.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to New York JFK route in September
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates and that JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. Ahern said the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is hard to beat, noting that it's easy and close. Dambeck acknowledged the industry's nature, saying air carriers will fluctuate based on demand and that JetBlue just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for.

Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said that route is performing well, with Boston seeing great demand. As for whether the JFK route could return in the future, Dambeck said the door is not closed. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.

cards.headline: Trump administration releases declassified records referencing Florida voter data collection
cards.teaser: Declassified intelligence records show a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter-registration information from commercial websites in 2022, though the records do not say Florida ballots or vote totals were altered.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump's national address Thursday renewed the debate over election security, while newly released intelligence records put a spotlight on publicly available Florida voter-registration data. Trump said during his Thursday address that mail-in ballots are inherently corrupt, urging Congress to adopt tighter voting restrictions and repeating claims about the 2020 election that have not been substantiated. Trump did not single out Florida, but records released by his White House did.

One declassified report says a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter-registration information from commercial websites in 2022. The same actor also obtained records from Colorado, Connecticut, Michigan, Oklahoma and Rhode Island. Another intelligence record lists Florida among 18 states whose voter information was obtained for possible identity matching and public-opinion analysis. The records describe the collection of voter information, some of it publicly available, but do not say Florida ballots or vote totals were altered. The 2022 report also says the actor's motive was unknown. The White House characterized the broader collection effort as a major compromise of American voter data. However, an earlier federal assessment of the 2022 elections found no evidence that detected foreign cyber activity prevented voting, changed votes or compromised the integrity of ballots.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County woman turns $20 scratch-off into $5 million jackpot
hero.body:
A St. Lucie County woman hit a $5 million jackpot earlier this year from a scratch-off lottery ticket, Florida Lottery officials announced Friday. Maria Duran, 57, claimed the top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6. She chose to receive her winnings as a one-time, lump-sum payment of $3,262,138.

Duran purchased her winning ticket from PK 2 Quick Mart, located at 4101 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce. The $20 scratch-off game offers overall odds of winning at 1-in-2.90.

The chance of winning the $5 million top prize playing this game is 1-in-4,018,135. The Florida Lottery released the information about Duran's win on Friday, several months after she claimed the prize in April.

The retailer that sold the winning ticket typically receives a bonus commission from the Florida Lottery for selling a top-prize winning scratch-off ticket. The $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH game remains available for purchase at Florida Lottery retailers.

cards.headline: Boynton Beach Fire Rescue saves dog from raw sewage lift station
cards.teaser: Boynton Beach Fire Rescue Department firefighters rescued a dog that fell 10 to 12 feet into a lift station holding about 2 feet of raw sewage Thursday.
cards.body:
A dog fell roughly 10 to 12 feet into a lift station holding about 2 feet of raw sewage Thursday, prompting a specialized confined space rescue by Boynton Beach Fire Rescue Department. Squad 6 crews arrived and assessed the scene before upgrading the incident to a Special Operations confined space rescue, the department said. Firefighters developed a rescue plan and had Firefighter Ramirez properly rigged and ready to enter the lift station.

From the time he went on air, Firefighter Ramirez rescued the dog and safely exited the lift station in just 4 minutes, the department said. Once above ground, crews decontaminated the dog and gave it oxygen before turning it over to Animal Control. Animal Control successfully reunited the dog with its owner, according to a Facebook post from the department.

cards.headline: Lake County sheriff pursues conviction in bank robbery case
cards.teaser: The Lake County sheriff is working to pursue a conviction in a bank robbery case.
cards.body:
The Lake County sheriff is pursuing a conviction in a bank robbery case. Law enforcement is moving forward with prosecution efforts in the robbery investigation.

The sheriff's office is handling the case as it proceeds through the criminal justice system. The bank robbery case remains under prosecution by Lake County authorities.

Officials are working to secure a conviction against the suspect or suspects involved in the bank robbery. The Lake County sheriff continues to pursue the case.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast residents report avoiding lettuce amid E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks
cards.teaser: Five confirmed cases of cyclospora have been reported locally since May, including two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County.
cards.body:
Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected by E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks linked to contaminated produce, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations, with confirmed cases also reported locally from the Palm Beaches into the Treasure Coast. According to the Florida Department of Health, there have been five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May: two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County, and one in Martin County. The outbreaks can cause severe stomach illness and intense diarrhea. Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are trying to stay away from lettuce. Jenny Rhodes said she misses her salads and berries but would rather be careful. George Lorenz said while grabbing lunch with his father Brian on Clematis Street in downtown West Palm Beach that he's heard it's going around and is trying to stay away from it. They got pizza from Elisabetta's instead. In Boynton Beach, Hendriette Peckens said she bought two big bags of oranges, bread, and some apples while avoiding produce because of the outbreak and planned to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner.

Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should stick to melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel, but you still want to wash them before you cut into them and peel them. That includes foods like bananas, melons, and avocados. She also recommends washing all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them and says beans and nuts are safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein. Barone's biggest warning is to avoid bagged lettuce if possible and instead buy whole heads of lettuce, peeling away the outer layers and avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly. She recommends cleaning produce using a one-to-three part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water, then soak, massage and clean off your produce and make sure to cook your vegetables.

hero.headline: Security ramped up for World Cup final Sunday in New Jersey
hero.teaser: Federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies are implementing security measures two years in the making for Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain.
hero.body:
A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. For Sunday's match, FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there is anything that needs to be done from a threat perspective.

The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security.

cards.headline: MLB restricts dugout iPads to prevent AI use in game decisions
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night to prevent artificial intelligence from helping make in-game decisions.
cards.body:
The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers that the custom tab had expanded the use of dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose.

The memo said the custom tab included recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches. A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations.

Sword wrote that instituting the prohibition beginning with the second half of the season provides clubs that relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead time to make any necessary adjustments. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple.

cards.headline: Photographer recalls baby Lamine Yamal bathed by teenage Messi ahead of World Cup final
cards.teaser: Barcelona photographer Joan Monfort took photos of teenage Lionel Messi bathing baby Lamine Yamal in 2007 for a charity calendar. The two now face off in Sunday's World Cup final.
cards.body:
Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for the Associated Press, took the photos in 2007 as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate. Her baby boy was paired up with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. A tearful Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later. The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in Sunday's World Cup final.

Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal was enjoying his international breakout and led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, and interest has skyrocketed with the World Cup final looming. Monfort, 58, is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey. He said his heart is split and he doesn't know if he wants Messi or Yamal to win. He has an everlasting love for the best player of all time in Messi, but Yamal has broken the mold and represents a new, diverse Spain, thanks to his parents from Morocco and Equatorial Guinea.

cards.headline: Argentina rallies past England 2-1 to reach World Cup final
cards.teaser: Argentina scored two late goals to defeat England 2-1 Wednesday and advance to the World Cup final, where they will face Spain on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
cards.body:
Trailing 1-0 going into the 85th minute, Argentina rallied for a 2-1 victory over England on Wednesday with goals from Enzo Fernandez and substitute Lautaro Martinez. England took the lead through Anthony Gordon's goal in the 55th minute, but Argentina refused to give in as they have done repeatedly throughout this World Cup. At the final whistle, Messi fell to his knees in celebration while England players collapsed in disbelief. Martinez said he dreamed it and told Alexis Mac Allister before the match that he was going to come on and win it. The defending champions will take on European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves while Mac Allister sent a header off the post as wave after wave of Argentina attacks came. Messi fed the ball to Fernandez to sweep in the equalizer from outside the box in the 85th minute. Two minutes into stoppage time, Messi sent in a cross for Martinez to head in the winner.

England lost in the World Cup semifinals for the third time after previous defeats to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018. Argentina has now extinguished English hopes at the World Cup in 1986, 1998 and 2026. England captain Harry Kane said he was gutted for the team, the staff and the fans, noting they worked so hard to be here and gave every bit of blood, sweat and tears. England coach Thomas Tuchel said Argentina played with more risk and rhythm, with the feeling they had nothing to lose anymore, which freed them up and held England back because they played with a feeling they had a lot to lose. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team proved the collectiveness and brotherhood they have and the fight to the very end.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Edge Palm Beach 3-2 in Extra Innings
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets opened the second half of the season with a 3-2 extra-inning win over the Palm Beach Cardinals on Friday night at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie scored
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets opened the second half of the season with a 3-2 extra-inning win over the Palm Beach Cardinals on Friday night at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie scored the deciding run in the top of the 10th before Miguel Mejias retired the Cardinals in order to close it out, giving the Mets a 1-0 lead in the three-game series.

Palm Beach struck first on a Sebastian Dos Santos solo home run in the bottom of the first. The early deficit was a tall order for St. Lucie, which came in 16-34 on the season when allowing the first run.

Randy Guzman answered in a hurry in his first game back from the injured list, where he had been since June 9. In his first at-bat, Guzman launched a 108 mph solo homer 374 feet to left to tie it at 1-1 in the second. It was his 10th home run of the season.

Palm Beach edged back ahead in the bottom of the second on a fielder's choice, but St. Lucie answered again when Elian Pena hit his fourth home run of the year to level the score at 2-2.

From there it became a pitchers' duel. Mets starter Joel Lara allowed two runs on four hits over 4 2/3 innings, walking three and striking out five. Zack Mack followed with 1 1/3 scoreless innings and two strikeouts, and Elwis Mijares handled the next three innings, allowing just two hits with no walks and three strikeouts. Mijares earned the win to improve to 4-4.

With the score still tied in the 10th, the Mets started the inning with automatic runner AJ Salgado at second. Branny De Oleo moved him to third with a sacrifice bunt, and Chase Meggers brought him home on a sacrifice fly for a 3-2 lead.

Mejias took the bottom of the 10th and delivered a perfect frame, striking out two before getting Matthew Miura to pop out to end it, earning his second save of the season.

The Mets improved to 7-13 in the second half and 40-46 overall. Palm Beach fell to 12-9 in the second half and 45-42 overall. St. Lucie can lock up the series Saturday night, with first pitch set for 6:30 p.m. at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

hero.headline: Boca Raton B'nai Torah Congregation TLC Program Offers Summer Service Projects for Families
hero.teaser: Families looking for ways to give back this summer can take part in the TLC Program at B'nai Torah Congregation, where volunteers help with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
hero.body:
The TLC Program at B'nai Torah Congregation, led by Summer Faerman, is part of the synagogue's broader effort to connect people of all ages with mitzvah opportunities or meaningful good deeds. The program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed and has helped make service a central part of synagogue life since 2012. B'nai Torah Congregation describes the TLC Program as a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida.

The congregation says the program focuses on hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations, special needs and other community concerns. Participants can volunteer in a variety of ways, including making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers say the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation.

The goal is to show service as something practical, welcoming and easy to begin. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. Families looking for ways to give back this summer can take part in hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors.

As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

hero.headline: Democratic Rep. Angie Nixon gets September trial date for Capitol sit-in charges
hero.teaser: State Rep. Angie Nixon will stand trial the week of September 21 on misdemeanor charges from her May sit-in outside the governor's office protesting Florida's congressional map.
hero.body:
Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon learned she will stand trial the week of September 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Nixon and other protesters occupied the area for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map, which could help Republicans add up to four seats in the U.S. House. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave. Nixon calls the prosecution political and has incorporated the case into her campaign for U.S. Senate.

The trial is scheduled after Florida's August 18 primary, in which Nixon is challenging retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman for the Democratic Senate nomination. Following Wednesday's hearing, Nixon said if they think the threat of a trial is going to make her back down, they picked the wrong woman. Vindman tightened his grip on the Democratic money lead during the second quarter, raising $8.5 million and pushing his total receipts above $16 million. Republican Sen. Ashley Moody reported raising another $3.6 million. The November special election will determine who serves the final two years of Marco Rubio's term after Moody was appointed to the Senate when Rubio resigned to become secretary of state.

cards.headline: Leon County jury orders Florida Rep. Fabian Basabe to pay $450,000 in sexual harassment case
cards.body:
A Leon County jury found Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation Friday, ordering him to pay $450,000 to former legislative aide Nicolas Frevola, former intern Jacob Cutbirth and Frevola's mother. Basabe represented himself in the civil trial despite having no legal training, a decision he later acknowledged was a mistake.

The trial was repeatedly interrupted by procedural mistakes and violations of court orders. Circuit Judge J. Lee Marsh told Basabe that if an attorney had committed half of the violations he did, they would have been sanctioned. Basabe told jurors he represented himself to demonstrate he had nothing to hide, but continues to deny the underlying allegations against him. He has not been criminally charged.

An outside ethics investigation previously conducted for the Florida House reached an inconclusive finding. Political opponents quickly called for Basabe's resignation following the verdict. The judgment could renew questions about whether House leaders will pursue disciplinary action against the lawmaker.

Basabe is seeking reelection this fall. The verdict adds to a week of courtroom developments for Florida lawmakers that also saw Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon receive a September 21 trial date on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Nixon was arrested after refusing to leave during a protest over Florida's newly approved congressional map.

cards.headline: Vindman raises $8.5 million in Florida Senate race as special election heats up
cards.teaser: Democrat Alex Vindman expanded his fundraising lead over rival Angie Nixon with $8.5 million raised in the second quarter, pushing total receipts above $16 million in the race for Marco Rubio's former seat.
cards.body:
Retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman tightened his grip on the Democratic money lead during the second quarter, raising $8.5 million and pushing his total receipts above $16 million in Florida's U.S. Senate race. Vindman said Republicans woke up Friday morning with a bit of a panic, adding there is no denying the Florida Senate race is in play. He is challenging state Rep. Angie Nixon for the Democratic nomination in the August 18 primary.

Republican Sen. Ashley Moody reported raising another $3.6 million during the same period. Her campaign promoted polling showing her leading either Vindman or Nixon in a potential general-election matchup. Moody was appointed to the Senate after Marco Rubio resigned to become secretary of state, and the November special election will determine who serves the final two years of Rubio's term. Nixon learned she will stand trial the week of September 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave during a protest over Florida's newly approved congressional map. Nixon calls the prosecution political and has incorporated the case into her Senate campaign.

cards.headline: South Florida residents avoid lettuce as E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks spread
cards.teaser: Thousands across the U.S. have been affected by contaminated produce outbreaks, with five confirmed local cyclospora cases in Palm Beach, St. Lucie and Martin counties since May.
cards.body:
Reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country as outbreaks of E. coli and cyclospora linked to lettuce, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations, prompt South Florida residents to change their diets. Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected, with confirmed cases reported locally from the Palm Beaches into the Treasure Coast. According to the Florida Department of Health, five confirmed local cases of cyclospora have been reported since May, with two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County. In Boynton Beach, shopper Hendriette Peckens said she bought two big bags of oranges, bread and some apples while avoiding produce and planning to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner.

Samantha Barone, a dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers and stick to melon, things that have a harder skin that you can peel. That includes foods like bananas, melons and avocados. She recommends washing all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them and said beans and nuts are safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein. Barone warned against bagged lettuce if possible, instead recommending buying whole heads of lettuce and peeling away the outer layers. She also advised avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly, and recommended cleaning produce using a one-to-three part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth backs Blue Angels low-altitude Pensacola flyover despite safety concerns
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth defended a Blue Angels jet that flew so low over a crowded Pensacola beach Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying, marking the third time he has intervened in military flyover investigations.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is sticking to encouraging low-altitude military flyovers after a Blue Angels fighter jet buzzed a Pensacola beach on Wednesday, raising new scrutiny after the Pentagon has dismissed a series of safety reviews of such flights. Video spreading widely on social media shows a jet from the Navy's demonstration squadron flying so low over a crowded beach that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears. The U.S. Navy said in a statement shortly afterward that it was conducting a thorough safety review. On Thursday morning, Hegseth wrote on his personal X account that the flyovers will continue until morale improves, without elaborating. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, a Trump administration political appointee, said the Navy had no problem with the flight and there would be no reprimands or firings. The Pentagon's top spokesman, Sean Parnell, wrote carry on patriots on social media alongside a photo showing a Blue Angels jet with a wingtip just feet above the heads of beachgoers.

It is at least the third time that Hegseth and others have voiced support for military aviators performing maneuvers that have drawn public scrutiny and military investigations. In two prior cases, Hegseth's remarks led to the end of safety investigations. Jeff Guzzetti, an aviation safety consultant who used to investigate crashes for both the National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration, said it is shocking that the top leaders of the military would excuse this type of reckless behavior. A cavalier attitude like that can only lead to accidents, he said.

cards.headline: Trump administration releases declassified records referencing Florida voter data collection
cards.teaser: Declassified intelligence records show a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter-registration information from commercial websites in 2022, though the records do not say Florida ballots or vote totals were altered.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump's national address Thursday renewed the debate over election security, while newly released intelligence records put a spotlight on publicly available Florida voter-registration data. Trump said during his Thursday address that mail-in ballots are inherently corrupt, urging Congress to adopt tighter voting restrictions and repeating claims about the 2020 election that have not been substantiated. Trump did not single out Florida, but records released by his White House did.

One declassified report says a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter-registration information from commercial websites in 2022. The same actor also obtained records from Colorado, Connecticut, Michigan, Oklahoma and Rhode Island. Another intelligence record lists Florida among 18 states whose voter information was obtained for possible identity matching and public-opinion analysis. The records describe the collection of voter information, some of it publicly available, but do not say Florida ballots or vote totals were altered. The 2022 report also says the actor's motive was unknown. The White House characterized the broader collection effort as a major compromise of American voter data. However, an earlier federal assessment of the 2022 elections found no evidence that detected foreign cyber activity prevented voting, changed votes or compromised the integrity of ballots.

cards.headline: Republican gubernatorial candidate Fishback faces court challenge over Florida residency requirement
cards.teaser: Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback will defend his eligibility to remain in the primary next week as opponent Jay Collins argues records showing Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., mean he does not satisfy Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governor.
cards.body:
Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback will defend his eligibility to remain in the primary during a two-day hearing scheduled to begin Tuesday in Tallahassee. Lt. Jay Collins, one of Fishback's opponents, argues that records showing Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., mean he does not satisfy Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governor. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida and maintained the state as his permanent home.

Because primary ballots have already been printed, the judge has said a ruling against Fishback could require election officials to post notices and decline to count votes cast for him. The case represents another looming legal fight over the Republican primary for governor.

hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap as needs outpace available money
hero.teaser: Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall, and the gap between what the county needs and what it can afford could shape how residents get around for decades.
hero.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next 20 years, a gap that could determine how residents travel for decades to come.

The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements through 2050, but only $701 million is currently available. That means the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Nearly all of the available funding comes from state and federal sources, with only $10 million coming from local revenue. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August and outlines transportation needs across roads, transit, aviation, freight, and other infrastructure categories.

Among the most pressing unfunded needs are nine roads the county identified as requiring widening as traffic grows. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, money that is not currently available, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. Without funding for these widening projects, the county will be unable to address growing congestion on these corridors.

State Road 710 stands out as among the county's highest priorities and has been the subject of repeated safety concerns. About $300 million in projects are planned for the corridor, reflecting the urgent need for improvements on this route. The massive funding shortfall highlights the challenge facing Martin County as it tries to balance transportation demands with limited financial resources over the coming decades.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce woman claims $5 million lottery jackpot from scratch-off ticket
hero.body:
Maria Duran, 57, of St. Lucie County claimed a $5 million top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6, Florida Lottery officials announced Friday. Duran chose to receive her winnings as a one-time, lump-sum payment of $3,262,138.

Duran purchased her winning ticket from PK 2 Quick Mart, located at 4101 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce. The $20 scratch-off game offers overall odds of winning of 1-in-2.90.

The chance of winning the $5 million top prize playing this game is 1-in-4,018,135, according to lottery officials. The game continues to be sold at retailers throughout Florida.

Florida Lottery officials released the information in a statement Friday, confirming the prize claim that occurred earlier this year. The PK 2 Quick Mart location on Okeechobee Road sold the winning ticket.

hero.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September after low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He explained that JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said. Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. Ahern said the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is hard to beat. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said.

Dambeck said JetBlue's Boston route is performing well and seeing great demand. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. As for whether the JFK route could return in the future, Dambeck said the door is not closed. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.
